rows.reason: No PEMS row of its own: C2 records r5 as a site-authored interpretation step and p.107#4 (badge EMT) as owned by r6. p.107#4 badges the EMT for acting on a STEMI 12-lead, not for interpreting one, so citing it here would authorise EMT interpretation that PEMS does not print.
rows.pems_text: If 12-Lead ECG reads “STEMI” or “ACUTE MI”, initiate transport to the nearest PCI capable hospital. Notify the receiving facility of a “Pre-Hospital STEMI Alert.”* Refer to PEMS Administrative Policy: STEMI Field Triage.
rows.note: p.107#4 is owned by site r6 (STEMI alert / notification). r5 is a site-authored interpretation step with no PEMS row of its own; PEMS badges the EMT for acting on the 12-lead, so the site's P-only gate is narrower than the source. Authoring question, no cell change.

rows.action: STEMI Alert / Notification: • Contact receiving facility via COR and provide "Pre-Hospital STEMI Alert" with patient's name and date of birth to facil
rows.pems_text: If 12-Lead ECG reads “STEMI” or “ACUTE MI”, initiate transport to the nearest PCI capable hospital. Notify the receiving facility of a “Pre-Hospital STEMI Alert.”* Refer to PEMS Administrative Policy: STEMI Field Triage.

rows.action: Extended ECG Assessment: • If 12-Lead ECG is indeterminate or high suspicion for cardiac ischemia, obtain serial ECGs at 10-minute intervals. • Contac
rows.pems_text: Contact Medical Control for guidance as needed. If 12-Lead ECG is indeterminate or there is high suspicion for cardiac ischemia, obtain serial ECGs at 10-minute intervals and contact Medical Control for guidance.

rows.action: IV/IO Access: • Establish IV / IO access when indicated (refer to Intraosseous Access procedure).
rows.reason: PEMS 2024 p.107 prints no IV/IO access row (access is p.231's procedure section and the arrest protocols); this page's row has no PEMS counterpart.

rows.action: Cardiac Monitoring: • Consider continuous cardiac monitoring.
rows.pems_text: Monitor cardiac rhythm. Refer to Tachyarrhythmias or Bradycardia protocol, as needed.
rows.binding_evidence: p.107#7 "Monitor cardiac rhythm. Refer to Tachyarrhythmias or Bradycardia protocol, as needed." badge I — the only cardiac-monitoring row printed for Chest Pain. The page had resolved the alignment as no-counterpart; the PEMS row is unambiguous.

rows.action: Aspirin Administration (for ACS/STEMI): • Aspirin (NSAID - inhibits platelet action preventing clot formation) • Indication: Acute coronary syndromes
rows.pems_text: Administer: ADULT: Aspirin 324 mg PO chewed

rows.action: Nitroglycerin Administration: • Administer Nitroglycerin per the Pain Control protocol for chest pain. • Confirm all "Rights" prior to administration.
rows.pems_text: If systolic blood pressure remains above 100 mmHg and MAP ≥ 65, consider: ADULT: Nitroglycerine 0.4 mg SL. May repeat every 5 minutes as needed for relief of chest pain, up to three doses.

rows.action: Analgesia: • Consider analgesia (refer to the Pain Control protocol).
rows.pems_text: Consider analgesia. Refer to Pain Control protocol.

rows.action: Medical Control Contact: • Contact Medical Control for guidance as needed.
rows.pems_text: Contact Medical Control for guidance as needed. If 12-Lead ECG is indeterminate or there is high suspicion for cardiac ischemia, obtain serial ECGs at 10-minute intervals and contact Medical Control for guidance.
rows.note: PEMS MC in every column; site MC in every column. Level already correct; goes to the split review list. Do not set to matched.

rows.action: Right-Sided / 15-Lead ECG: • Consider right-sided 12-Lead or 15-Lead ECG for additional assessment.
rows.reason: PEMS 2024 p.107 prints no right-sided / 15-lead ECG row; serial 12-leads appear inside the MC-badged p.107#9, and no row authorises a 15-lead.

rows.action: Universal Patient Care / Initial Patient Contact: • Follow the Universal Patient Care / Initial Patient Contact protocol. • Ensure scene safety and ut
rows.pems_text: Follow Universal Patient Care / Initial Patient Contact protocol.

rows.action: Primary Assessment: • Perform Primary and Secondary Survey. • Obtain complete set of vital signs including bilateral BP if possible. • Assess for sign
rows.reason: PEMS 2024 p.109 prints no primary/secondary-survey or vital-signs row; its six rows are cross-references and the MC contact row. Local authoring.

rows.action: Stroke Assessment: • Perform stroke screening (Cincinnati Prehospital Stroke Scale or equivalent). • If stroke is suspected, refer to the Stroke / TIA
rows.pems_text: If stroke is suspected, refer to Stroke / TIA protocol.

rows.action: Cardiac Assessment: • Assess for chest pain, pressure, or symptoms consistent with acute coronary syndrome. • Obtain 12-lead ECG if available. • If AC
rows.pems_text: If the patient is experiencing chest pain / discomfort, or symptoms consistent with an acute coronary syndrome, refer to Chest Pain (Cardiac) protocol.

rows.action: Respiratory Assessment: • Assess for respiratory distress, pulmonary edema, or hypoxia. • Apply pulse oximetry and administer oxygen as indicated. • I
rows.pems_text: If the patient is experiencing respiratory distress, refer to Airway Management and Ventilatory Support procedure and Respiratory Distress protocol.

rows.action: Glucose Assessment: • Check blood glucose level. • If hyperglycemia or hypoglycemia is present or suspected, refer to the Hyperglycemia / Hypoglycemia
rows.pems_text: Check blood glucose level. Refer to Hyperglycemia / Hypoglycemia protocol.

rows.action: Medical Control Consultation: • Contact Medical Control for guidance on blood pressure management as needed. • Do NOT attempt to aggressively lower bl
rows.pems_text: Contact Medical Control for guidance as needed.

rows.action: Begin high-quality CPR / determine DNR status
rows.pems_text: Determine DNR status. Refer to Death and Criteria for Withholding Resuscitation protocol.

rows.action: Consider spinal motion restriction
rows.pems_text: Consider spinal motion restriction.

rows.action: Establish IV/IO (Humeral IO preferred)
rows.pems_text: Obtain IV/IO access (humeral IO preferred is IV unavailable).

rows.action: Fluid Resuscitation: 0.9% Sodium Chloride up to 1 L (Adult) / 20 mL/kg (Ped)
rows.pems_text: Administer: ADULT: 0.9% Sodium Chloride IV/IO up to 1 L in 250 – 500 mL boluses PEDIATRIC: 0.9% Sodium Chloride 20 mL/kg IV/IO Repeat as needed to maintain adequate perfusion, up to 60 mL/kg total.

rows.action: Defibrillation: 200 J Biphasic / 360 J Monophasic (Adult) / 2 J/kg initial, 4 J/kg subsequent (Ped) (AED for EMR/EMT, Manual for I/P)
rows.reason: p.63#7 is the compound row named in this card as an unresolved inline badge contradiction: PEMS prints one badge (I) on "If VF or VT is present, or AED is advising to shock [EMR], immediately defibrillate". The page's own row text "(AED for EMR/EMT, Manual for I/P)" encodes both levels, so neither I nor EMT is the whole answer. audit/level-scan/badge-overrides.yaml is still empty.
rows.pems_text: If VF or VT is present, or AED is advising to shock [EMR], immediately defibrillate: ADULT: 200 joules Biphasic / 360 joules Monophasic, or manufacturer’s recommendation. PEDIATRIC: 2 joules/kg initial, 4 joules/kg subsequent After each defibrillation, perform 2 minutes of CPR, followed by rhythm assessment. If VF / VT persists, defibrillate again, then consider medication therapy as listed below.

rows.action: Epinephrine 1 mg (0.1mg/mL) IV/IO (Adult) / 0.01 mg/kg IV/IO (Ped) q3-5 mins
rows.pems_text: Administer: ADULT: Epinephrine 1 mg IV/IO [0.1 mg/mL concentration] PEDIATRIC: Epinephrine 0.01 mg/kg IV/IO [0.1 mg/mL concentration] Repeat every 3-5 minutes during cardiac arrest.

rows.action: First Antiarrhythmic: Amiodarone 300 mg IV/IO (Adult) / 5 mg/kg (Ped max 300mg) OR Lidocaine 1 mg/kg IV/IO (Adult max 100mg, Ped max 50mg)
rows.pems_text: If VF / VT persists, administer: ADULT: Amiodarone (Cordarone) 300 mg IV/IO slow push PEDIATRIC: Amiodarone (Cordarone) 5 mg/kg IV/IO slow push. Maximum dose 300 mg. OR, if Amiodarone is unavailable, administer: ADULT: Lidocaine (Xylocaine) 1 mg/kg IV/IO slow push. Maximum dose 100 mg. PEDIATRIC: Lidocaine (Xylocaine) 1 mg/kg IV/IO slow push. Maximum dose 50 mg.

rows.action: Second Antiarrhythmic: Amiodarone 150 mg IV/IO (Adult) / [MC] 5 mg/kg (Ped max 150mg) OR Lidocaine 0.5 mg/kg IV/IO (Adult max 100mg) / 1 mg/kg (Ped ma
rows.pems_text: If VF / VT persists, ensure optimal defibrillator pad placement, then administer: ADULT: Amiodarone (Cordarone) 150 mg IV/IO slow push PEDIATRIC: [Contact Medical Control] Amiodarone (Cordarone) 5 mg/kg IV/IO slow push. Maximum dose 150 mg. OR, if Amiodarone is unavailable, administer: ADULT: Lidocaine (Xylocaine) 0.5 mg/kg IV/IO slow push. Maximum dose 100 mg. PEDIATRIC: Lidocaine (Xylocaine) 1 mg/kg IV/IO slow push. Maximum dose 50 mg.

rows.action: Persistent VF/VT: Magnesium Sulfate 2 g IV/IO (Adult) / [MC] 40 mg/kg (Ped max 2g)
rows.pems_text: If VF / VT persists, administer: ADULT: Magnesium Sulfate 2 g IV/IO slow push PEDIATRIC: [Contact Medical Control] Magnesium Sulfate 40 mg/kg IV/IO slow push. Maximum dose 2 g.

rows.action: Dialysis/Crush/Hyperkalemia: Calcium Chloride 1 g IV/IO (Adult) / 20 mg/kg (Ped max 1g) THEN flush THEN Sodium Bicarbonate 50 mEq IV/IO (Adult) / 1 mE
rows.pems_text: For cardiac arrest in renal dialysis patients, patients with crush injuries, suspected calcium channel blocker overdose or hyperkalemia only, also administer (preferably via separate lines): ADULT: Calcium Chloride 1 g IV/IO slow push Followed by 20 mL 0.9% sodium chloride flush ADULT: Sodium Bicarbonate 50 mEq IV/IO slow push PEDIATRIC: Calcium Chloride 20mg/kg (max dose 1g) IV/IO slow push Followed by 20 mL 0.9% sodium chloride flush PEDIATRIC: Sodium Bicarbonate 1 mEq/kg (max dose 50 mEq) IV/IO slow push Repeat in 5 minutes if no change.

rows.action: Proceed to Post ROSC Care if pulses return
rows.pems_text: If return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) is achieved, refer to Cardiac Arrest: Post ROSC Care.

rows.action: Contact Medical Control for guidance / termination of resuscitation
rows.pems_text: Contact Medical Control for guidance as needed. See Pearls below regarding Termination of Resuscitation.
